chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: Locked out of studio work; Rainbow Grill with Joe Williams and Bobby Hackett
summary: He missed TV and studio jobs, disliked the politics, watched rock groups replace older players, and recalls the Rainbow Grill with Joe Williams and the Riverboat with Bobby Hackett.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Then we did a few things, but in the meantime I was right there with the club date scene too. You see. And, eventually, I could see that things were not working too well, because I was not in the television scene or the transcription scene, I was not in that. So I had to do the best I could, 'cause at that time if you were in a studio band you made $280 a week and that went on for 52 weeks, you know what I mean. Then there were other things that they could do.
Did you try to get into that?

Yeah. I tried. But I just didn't like the atmosphere and politics and etcetera, you know, I don't have that kind of a temperament, you know. Some people are atuned to these things and some people aren't, you see. But I was workin', but you know I could see things...and then things went bad for...you know, they were hirin' musicians to play for these rock and roll singers and groups and they were usin' all jazz musicians, then finally, what broke

that up is that groups, they had their own band, so they didn't need the guys, older experienced musicians, to back 'em up. And then all the studio stuff went to the coast, so that broke that up, see. It was just one of those things. But I could see all these things happening, you know what I mean. So there was nothing you could do about these things. I had a couple of good jobs. I had a nice...I think it was eight weeks at the Rainbow Grill, the 65th floor of the Rockefeller Plaza with Joe Williams. I had the quartet behind him and that was a beautiful job. That was one of the best jobs I had, other than Cafe Society, in New York. I mean where you could just be free to go ahead and blow and you had people comin' in from all parts of the country, just because they wanted to look out over the skyline of New York, from the Rainbow Grill, you see. And so you got a chance to expand. And then I did some things with Bobby Hackett at the Riverboat. And that was a nice experience. And those were the two nicest experiences (I had during this period).
